newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked bonds end up in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked bonds end up in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli inflation-linked bonds closed higher on Wednesday in active trading but traders said the market has reached equilibrium at the current price range.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.03 pct to 172.94
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 162.93.
Volume was high at 196 million shekels with activity in the Makams rising to 83 million shekels.

"The market is in a wait-and-see position. The government will have to raise money soon. This can be done by raising taxes or by issuing bonds. The issuing of a new series of bonds would have a strong impact on the market," said one trader.

CPI-linked bonds continued to rise today but the market was very quiet and is likely to remain so for the time being, the trader said. "Institutional investors were very active buyers during the last month, but I believe that in the near future they will reduce their activity," he said.
"After three difficult years the mutual funds can show positive results. The market will stabilize now and remain at current levels," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.
Traders said unlinked bonds and Makams were stable because yields had reached a ceiling.
Dollar-linked bonds closed slightly lower in thin trading.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
